intent: Compare the value trends of YouTube and Television over relative time using the provided data.

Compare the value trends of YouTube and Television over relative time

accept: every listed area, reference mark, segment, or category is visible
each mark is correctly bound to its entity or series identity
reject: missing any required area, reference mark, segment, or category

units.claim: All 1 required area marks are present in Television: Television.
accept: every listed area, reference mark, segment, or category is visible

reject: missing any required area, reference mark, segment, or category

units.claim: YouTube's value generally increases over relative time, rising from 0 € at the start to 120 € at the end, with a minor dip around x≈0.51.
accept: YouTube value rises overall from 0 to 120 €
YouTube shows an upward trend with a small dip near the middle

units.claim: Television's value generally decreases over relative time, falling from a peak of 353.4 € near the start to 57 € at the end, with a brief rebound around x≈0.38.
accept: Television value falls overall from about 353 € to 57 €
Television shows a downward trend with a small rebound

optional_valid: YouTube ends at 120 € while Television ends at 57 €, so YouTube finishes higher.
Television's maximum value (353.4 €) is much larger than YouTube's maximum (120 €).
Both series start at 0 € at relative time 0.
unsupported_to_avoid: YouTube and Television are plotted on the same y-axis scale.
The two panels share a common vertical scale.
Television's value is always above YouTube's value.
The area sizes are directly comparable across panels.
The data represent a continuous time series rather than a snapshot.
review_notes: The intent asks to compare trends, so one trend unit per entity is used rather than separate endpoint or extremum units.
Panel identity is preserved: YouTube and Television are separate panels with their own y-axis ranges.
